newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain 1998 budget forecasts 3.5% GDP, 2.0% CPI-CiU.
newsitem.headline: Spain 1998 budget forecasts 3.5% GDP, 2.0% CPI-CiU.

text.p: The Spanish government's ally, Catalan Convergencia i Unio (CiU), said on Thursday that the 1998 Spanish budget would be based on a forecast of nominal economic growth of 5.5 percent.

CiU economic spokesman Francesc Homs told Reuters in a interview that next year's budget would be based on the forecast of real gross domestic product growth of 3.5 percent, while the consumer inflation target will be set at 2.0 percent.

He said this budget law is again aimed at securing Spain's prompt entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU). The budget must be presented in September and be approved before countries will be selected, based on 1997 economic data, to join the EMU launch.

"This is the last budget before the final decision will be taken. CiU really look for the peseta to enter the third phase of the monetary union. So we'll take all necessary measures to guarantee convergence with Europe," he said.
The ruling minority Popular Party government needs the CiU's legislative votes to pass the budget. The CiU backs the PP in an alliance but is not part of the government.
